title: complaint
description:
One synthetic cybercrime or fraud complaint.

A complaint is a citizen's account of what happened. It is evidence that somebody reported something, not evidence that it occurred, and nothing in the platform treats a named account as guilty because a complaint named it.

narrative_raw is the one field that holds free text written by a person. It is normalised for correlation and is never returned in a list view, an error, a log line or an export.

reported_at.description: When the complaint was filed. The correlation window is anchored on it, so a wrong value silently changes which transfers are considered.

category.description: A free-text label rather than an enum, because complaint taxonomies differ between sources and forcing one would lose the distinction the source drew.

transaction_reference.description: The transfer the complainant named, if they named one. This is what makes a tier-1 correlation: an exact reference match needs no confidence score and no review, because it is an identity rather than an inference.

suspected_account_id.description: The account the complainant suspects. A suspicion, recorded as one. It raises an alert for a person to look at and takes no action against the account.

metadata_json.description: Free-form synthetic context. Sanitised on ingestion: keys that look like secrets, tokens, raw identifiers, ground-truth labels, scenario ids or ring ids are dropped rather than stored.
